summary: Phase F backend tests (Reviews module — QR tokens + Google Business Locations sync) — 37/37 pytest cases PASS. Verified: (1) admin QR generate returns correct shape (id starts qr_, 10-char lowercase/digit token, review_url contains /r/{token}, ~90d default expiry), list is DESC-sorted with review_url on every item, PNG image endpoint returns real 8-byte PNG signature (>500 bytes), 404 for unknown token, DELETE removes token and subsequent public GET is 404. (2) Public /api/r/{token} returns customer+product+order context; POST creates a Review with source='QR', published=false, verified=true, product_id/order_number copied from token, and marks the token used (with used_at + review_id linkage) — reuse yields 410, subsequent GET yields 410. Validation: rating<1/>5 → 400, text<5 chars → 400, missing name → Pydantic 422. Expiry (forced via mongosh) yields 410 on both GET & POST. (3) Google locations CRUD works (401 without Bearer on every endpoint, list includes seeded gbl_01/gbl_02, POST returns id starting gbl_, PATCH updates, DELETE removes). Mocked sync of gbl_01 returns mocked:true, imported≥1, updated:0 on first call, total_reviews_fetched=5, location_rating float, review_count≥100 — after which the location's last_synced_at/rating/review_count are persisted and public /api/reviews returns only rating≥4 mocked reviews (verified=true); rating<4 mock reviews stay published=false. Idempotency verified (second call: imported=0, updated≥1). sync-all excludes inactive locations and returns per-location result envelopes. (4) Regression sanity: /api/products (paginated), /api/blog (published only), /api/instagram (active only), /api/analytics/track, HOPE10 coupon all still work. All test-created QR tokens, google-locations, and gmock_ reviews cleaned up via session-scoped mongosh teardown; seeded gbl_01/02 sync stats reset to defaults.

minor.issue: Mock generator picks 5 items via random.sample from a 7-item pool. In edge cases where the sample yields all rating=5, no rating<4 reviews are produced — which is fine but means the 'unpublished low-rating' assertion is only exercised on runs where sample includes a 4-star entry. Also: mocked responses always overwrite the location's rating on every call (idempotency test still passes because google_review_id is stable, but rating fluctuates on each sync since ratings are computed as round(sum/len) of the random subset).
Returns 200 (not 201) on create. Not a bug but 201 is more RESTful.
Returns {ok:true} even when token does not exist (no 404). Idempotent-by-design; matches DELETE /api/admin/locations convention.
Also returns 200 (not 201). Same convention as other create endpoints in this codebase.

action_items: None blocking — all Phase F acceptance criteria verified end-to-end.
(Optional) Return 201 on POST /api/admin/reviews/qr/generate and POST /api/admin/google-locations for REST correctness.
(Optional) Return 404 from DELETE /api/admin/reviews/qr/{token} (and DELETE /api/admin/google-locations/{gid}) when the id/token doesn't exist, so callers can distinguish 'deleted' vs 'not found'.

(Design/consistency) The mocked Google sync path always overwrites `rating` and `review_count` even if they came from a prior real API call. If a real API key is ever added later, running the mocked path first could clobber real data; consider only updating those fields when result['mocked'] is False, or store mocked stats under a separate key.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1963 lines — still well over the 700-line soft cap and up another ~540 lines in Phase F. Strongly recommend splitting: reviews_qr.py, google_locations.py, blog.py, instagram.py, analytics.py, sheets_import.py, locations.py, bulk_upload.py, orders.py, admin.py.

public_qr_submit stores payload.photos as-is (List[str]) without any URL/base64 validation or size cap. A caller could POST 1000 photo URLs (or 100MB of base64 data-URIs) and the whole array is persisted. Consider (a) capping len(photos) to e.g. 6, (b) rejecting anything >2KB per entry, and (c) validating http(s) scheme.
public_qr_submit: `payload.email` is not validated as an email. Pydantic's EmailStr would give a 422 on garbage input.

public_qr_submit: no rate limiting. A leaked token can be spam-submitted (well, only once due to 'used' guard) — but /api/r/{token} GET can be enumerated freely. Consider adding basic IP-based rate limiting or a captcha for the POST.

sync_google_location: `Review(**rv_doc).model_dump()` re-creates the model to attach a new id/timestamp on insert path — but on the update path, `rv_doc` (a plain dict) is `$set`-merged into the existing review, silently OVERWRITING `published` on every re-sync. If an admin manually unpublished a synced review, the next sync would re-publish it. Consider only setting fields that came from Google and preserving admin's `published` decision on updates.

sync_google_location: `Review(**rv_doc)` on the insert path receives a `source` field that may be the location's `label` — but the frontend/other endpoints may filter by source='Google'. Since seeded location labels are 'Mumbai — Design Center' etc., the source field will contain human-readable strings with em-dashes, which may break simple string filters and complicate CSV exports.

_fetch_google_reviews mocked path: `review_count` = 148 + random(0..50) — this fluctuates on every sync (idempotency test still passes because google_review_id is stable, but the location's review_count value changes each call). Should be deterministic per place_id or cached.
_fetch_google_reviews mocked path: `rating` = round(sum/len, 1). If admin syncs multiple times, the location rating jumps around 4.0..5.0. Persist a stable value or seed random with hash(place_id).
qr_generate: while-loop for token uniqueness has no bounded retry — with a 36^10 keyspace it's effectively infinite, but a bug (e.g. missing unique index) could hang. Add a max-attempts guard.

There is no unique index on `qr_tokens.token` — the while-loop guards against collisions but two concurrent generate requests could still race and both insert the same token. Add `db.qr_tokens.create_index('token', unique=True)` in startup_event, and handle DuplicateKeyError.
public_qr_info leaks `customer_email` in a public (no-auth) response. Anyone with the token URL can see the email address. Consider redacting to `a***@example.com` for the public info payload.

GoogleBusinessLocation model uses `min_rating_to_publish: int = 4` but rating can be a float from Google — comparison `rv['rating'] >= 4` works, but if admin sets `min_rating_to_publish = 4.5` via PATCH (dict body accepts anything), the int-typed field would truncate/reject. Consider `float` type.
update_google_location accepts arbitrary `dict` payload without Pydantic validation — same issue as update_location (Phase D). Recommend a `GoogleBusinessLocationUpdate` Pydantic model.

sync_all_google_locations catches HTTPException but not generic Exception — a network timeout or JSON parse error inside _fetch_google_reviews would abort the whole sync-all. Wrap the inner call in try/except Exception with a per-location error record.

The regex `if all(c.islower() or c.isdigit() for c in d['token'])` in _gen_token uses random.choices which is NOT cryptographically secure — fine for review tokens (unguessable at 36^10) but consider `secrets.token_urlsafe`/`secrets.choice` for a defense-in-depth improvement.
test_credentials: Admin session minted via mongosh at test-session start (see /app/memory/test_credentials.md). Fresh Bearer token per pytest session, cleaned by supervisor DB TTL.
seed_data_creation: During the test session the suite creates: 6 QR tokens (all deleted in teardown), 2 pytest google-locations (Pytest Branch + Pytest Inactive — both deleted mid-test/in teardown), and ~10 gmock_* reviews across gbl_01/gbl_02 (all deleted in teardown). Also resets seeded gbl_01/gbl_02 last_synced_at/rating/review_count back to null/0 so the DB is left in a pristine post-seed state. Verified via post-run mongosh: 0 pytest QR tokens, 0 gmock reviews, 0 pytest google-locations remain; both seeded locations (gbl_01, gbl_02) intact with stats cleared.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: `export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://wear-interactive.preview.emergentagent.com && cd /app/backend && set -a && source .env && set +a && python -m pytest tests/test_phase_f_reviews_qr_google.py -v -n 0 --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/phase_f_results.xml`. Force `-n 0` (serial) — tests share module-level cleanup lists and a STATE dict for cross-test token reuse. Seeded google-location place_ids are `ChIJXX_MockedMumbai_XX` / `ChIJXX_MockedErnakulam_XX` (NOT the internal ids gbl_01/gbl_02) — cleanup regex uses `^gmock_` which matches both. HOPE10 coupon validation requires BOTH `code` AND `subtotal` in the body (Pydantic CouponValidate).
rca of the issue: N/A — no backend bugs surfaced. Initial run had 3 test-side flakes: (1) sync_first_call assumed the mock ids used location id (`gbl_01`) but they actually use the seeded place_id (`ChIJXX_MockedMumbai_XX`) — fixed cleanup regex and lookup, (2) sync-all cleanup used `raw.splitlines()[-1]` which throws IndexError when mongosh returns empty output — added a defensive `if raw` guard, (3) HOPE10 coupon test omitted the required `subtotal` field → 422 — added `subtotal: 2000` to the payload. All three were test infra, not app bugs.
